alternatives_considered.approach: Fix formatMinor by formatting the signed whole part but special-casing whole === 0n to prefix a hardcoded '-'
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A hardcoded hyphen can disagree with the locale minus sign; deriving the minus part from the same pinned formatter is equally short and cannot disagree.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix readMembers with an aliased self-join of the members table (one alias for authorisation, one for the listing)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Drizzle aliases for a self-join add import and naming surface for one call site; the existing memberOfGroup EXISTS predicate already expresses exactly this authorisation and is already used for the write path, so reusing it keeps one spelling of the rule.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix RemoveButton by navigating away (router.push) like LeaveButton instead of refreshing in place

work_order.approach: Fix the four product defects in place with the smallest change that removes each root cause, and add regression tests at the level that can see each defect. formatMinor carries the sign outside the whole part: format the absolute whole through Intl, substitute the fraction, then prepend the formatter's own minus part when the input was negative. readMembers becomes one query: the member-list SELECT constrained by the existing memberOfGroup EXISTS predicate, returning null when it yields no rows. RemoveButton gains useRouter and mirrors ArchiveButton: on state.ok it calls router.refresh() and renders an in-place 'Removed <name>.' status with the button disabled — inserted (and announced) before the async refresh lands, with the row's disappearance as the durable signal. RenameGroupForm gains useRouter and calls router.refresh() when state.ok arrives so the surrounding server components re-render, keeping the existing field-sync and focus effects untouched. The refreshes are progressive enhancement only: both confirms are real form submits, so the no-JS path still works through the Server Action's own re-render. The archive-button planning gap is not a code change, and the SettingsForm instance of the same revalidate-without-refresh shape is deferred as its own ticket rather than fixed here.
assumptions: Intl en-US currency formatToParts of a negative value carries a 'minusSign' part ('-' prefix for EUR, JPY, BHD and INR — executed during planning); the fix reads that part from the same formatter and falls back to '-'.
router.refresh() re-renders the members page server components after revalidatePath('/', 'layout'), as ArchiveButton and LeaveNotice already rely on.

A member's own active row is returned by the constrained list query, so an empty result means the caller is not a member; the owner-cannot-leave and never-delete-rows invariants keep every group non-empty.
No call site depends on formatMinor dropping the sign for sub-unit negatives; all current call sites format literal 0n balances in this piece.
Component tests run against a hoisted shared router mock so refresh/push assertions observe the same fns the components called.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The money root cause was executed, not just read: the current algorithm's before-table (-5n EUR->'€0.05', -5n BHD->'BHD 0.005' with no minus) and the Intl minusSign probes for four currencies confirm both the defect and the fix's minus source. The other three defects were verified at their exact lines and each fix follows an in-repo precedent (ArchiveButton refresh, memberOfGroup predicate). What would move the number up is browser QA confirming the inserted removal status is announced before the refresh unmounts the row; what would move it down is a currency whose en-US minus layout is not a simple prefix, or a Drizzle type rejection of the EXISTS predicate in the SELECT where clause.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique changed the plan in five places and was overruled in two. Accepted: AC-2 restated as the observable behaviour (the 'single query' clause is not observable through the named integration tests, and TR-1's own proof is behavioural); AC-4 split into a members-page check and a home-after-navigation check; the router mock fixed with hoisted shared spies (the current mock mints a fresh vi.fn() per useRouter() call, so the planned refresh assertions could never pass); the empty-means-non-member assumption restated around the caller's own row rather than the owner row; reproduced set to true with an executed before-table and a BHD sub-unit case added (the JPY case guards only the whole-yen path the current code already handles). Rejected with reasons: (1) the demand for a list-level live region surviving the refresh — the unmount fact is correct, but the status insertion commits before the async refresh lands so it is still announced, the row's disappearance is the durable signal per the ui.md update-in-place pattern, and lifting confirmation state above the list is a rebuild disproportionate to this ticket, so the plan keeps the row-internal status, asserts its insertion in tests, and records the transience as a residual risk; (2) fixing SettingsForm here — the same-shape diagnosis is correct (verified: no useRouter, revalidate layout, server-read TopBar name), but it is a sixth finding outside the issue's five with TR-12 absent from acceptance, and per the ship-on-its-own test it is deferred in out_of_scope as its own ticket rather than widening this one.
evidence: Executed current algorithm in node: -5n EUR->'€0.05', -1n->'€0.01', -99n->'€0.99', -100n->'-€1.00', -1234n->'-€12.34', -5n BHD->'BHD 0.005' (no minus), -5n JPY->'-¥5' — confirms the sub-unit sign drop and that JPY negatives already work.
Executed Intl probes: formatToParts(-5n) carries minusSign:'-' as a prefix for EUR/JPY/BHD/INR en-US while formatToParts(0n) carries none — confirms the root cause and the fix's minus source.

validated_work_order.approach: Fix the two QA-proven root causes with different approaches from attempt 1, and carry forward that attempt's two passing fixes unchanged. BUG-1: Field generates its input id from the field name alone (field-${name}), so the members page renders two inputs with id field-name and fills/submits hit the wrong one. Field now derives a unique id per instance with React useId so each label targets exactly its own input; RenameGroupForm keeps its state.ok refresh effect, which becomes observable once the submit is fixed. BUG-2: RemoveButton called router.refresh() in the awaited continuation of the wrapped Server Action, before useActionState commits the ok state that renders the status. RemoveButton now follows the ArchiveButton precedent exactly: the wrapped action only returns the result, and a useEffect on state.ok commits the 'Removed <name>.' status render first and then calls router.refresh() once (announced-ref guarded). The money sign-carry and readMembers EXISTS-predicate fixes from attempt 1 passed QA (T-1, T-2) and are carried forward unchanged.

validated_work_order.root_cause: Two wrong diagnoses in attempt 1, both proven by QA evidence. (1) Rename: the plan blamed a missing router.refresh, but QA captured the Server Action request carrying the field's INITIAL value on the base commit — refresh can never fix a submit that sends the wrong value. The true cause is a duplicate DOM id: Field builds id as field-${name}, and the members page renders two Field name='name' inputs, so fills land in the placeholder field and Save submits the rename form's untouched value with a false 'Saved.'. (2) Removal: the plan assumed the status insertion commits before the async refresh lands, but the PR calls router.refresh() in the action's awaited continuation BEFORE useActionState commits the ok state — on a fast connection the refresh wins and the row unmounts with zero insertions, exactly QA's intermittent signature.

validated_work_order.understanding: Attempt 1 (previous-work-order.json v1, PR #21) was wrong on both browser defects, and QA's evidence proves it. First, the plan diagnosed rename staleness as a missing router.refresh(); but QA captured the Server Action body carrying the INITIAL name on base commit 7390e3e, and the T-7/T-4 trees show the typed value in the placeholder 'Name' input while the rename input kept the old value with a false 'Saved.'. The true cause is Field's id = field-${name} colliding across the two same-named fields on the members page. Second, the plan assumed the 'Removed' insertion commits before the refresh; but the PR dispatches router.refresh() in the wrapped action's continuation before useActionState commits ok state, so the refresh intermittently wins (T-9/T-10/T-11). The money and readMembers fixes passed QA and are carried forward; only the Field-id and removal-ordering approaches change.
